meta_thesis: The game is decided at minute 15-20, and the urn (earn) fight determines hero strength more than anything else — this is the biggest 6v6 urn team-fight meta of all time. Because winning hard early hands the enemy a comeback urn (50% armor in a 60-meter radius), early-game comps that stomp lane actually lose; competitive teams that won early lost almost every game. So the tier list is effectively an urn-fight tier list: AoE, CC, and front-line HP value dominate, single-target and pure-lane heroes fall.

hero_claims.why: Good but mediocre on the urn with better frontliners available; would move to A if the urn gets nerfed.
One of the best pre-10-minute heroes, but that no longer matters because stomping early gives the enemy the comeback urn. Only real value is Reposte cancelling Seven/McGinnis/Lash.
Below average this patch; beam build is too easily counterable versus other ults, and he floats near 45% win rate.
Best frontliner this patch. Buffs plus the global health reduction and buffed Spirit Snatch let one slam gain ~900 HP on the urn, stacking to 5-6k HP with 40 armor — an elite Heroic Aura holder.
Garbage: lowest utility of any hero in mid-boss/urn fights, no CC, doesn't kill through the health pool. Would likely be decent if the urn meta were changed.
Bottom of S/A. One of the best urn runners and urn fighters with AoE damage/amp, a bouncing ball, four abilities, mobility, and giga-late scaling.
Still very, very good and worth playing, but no longer Z-tier / top-five this patch.
Not great but better than Calico, with real individual-duel strength; melee changes plus the Spirit Snatch buff make his damage solid.
Framed as OP but is actually bait: Black Hole gets countered by McGinnis ult one-framing him, Lash ults him off, Dispel/Sinclair/Vyper outvalue him. Not picked once across competitive regions.
Simply a good hero this patch, per the creator.

Low-elo players call it S but in competitive it's roughly unpicked; worst early game in the game, and McGinnis does the same job far better (60% vs 52% win rate at E6). Bottom of A when balancing comp and pubs.
Garbage this patch — brings nothing valuable to urn fights; was OP one week ago, now the build gets swatted instantly.
Actually decent, not bad at all, carried by the Magic Carpet buff.

Top of C — fine and playable but countered by every top-seven hero. A floor-is-lava hero that loses value as ELO rises (less time on the ground) and gets cleansed by the multiple Dispel Magics per team in high ELO.
Solid, one of the better decent supports for this meta — a good circle hero in a circle meta.
Really good right now because you can dome the urn, but the creator calls that a bug likely hotfixed within 48 hours; his tier drops if fixed.
Giga fell off: not a snipe-lane meta and the urn is bad for her, though she snaps back up the moment the urn bug is fixed.

Broken always, averaging A+ every patch and inflated — a bad one-trick still wins over 50%. Good early/mid/late, flies, high HP, strong teamfight and 1v1; Spirit build benefited from the slam and Mystic Shot buffs.

Actually broken: maxed ult at the first urn fight one-frames a full-HP Dynamo even through Unstoppable, takes no skill (controller top damage), and has no counterplay. The turrets aren't the problem — the ult is.
Pretty mid, possibly underrated/balanced, but not enough games seen to be convinced.

The best hero in the game who lacks an OP urn fight, so the urn meta drags his placement down; if the urn mattered less he'd be giga-broken. Single-target in an AoE meta, yet went 2-13 in one comp run and still got picked 15 times.
Not bad but hard to place; would climb if the urn became a king-of-the-hill that can't complete with enemies inside, letting him stack his one plus Scorn/Burrow.
Valued very low and completely unplayed in tourney and high ELO; a victim hero that just explodes, strictly worse than Rem who has an escape/heal.

Z-tier turbo broken. Alchemical Fire + Echo Shard bomb does ~70k damage in grand finals, swaps people off the urn, dominates mid boss, stalls, and wins early/mid/late; the Mystic Shot buff is massive for her.
Broken: banned 38 of ~40 tourney games, and in the two he wasn't banned he was the best character in the lobby. Affliction is the core problem.
Really good value, arguably as strong as Doorman. Strong teamfight healing with the bouncing-burst buff, great ult for fights, three is good for pre-fight wave clear.
Should be and is good, but wants to see more; S+ in Phantom-and-below, less fun/unclear in Eternus. Apollo's Reposte can cancel him.
Still pretty broken with so much damage; the new Arctic Blast changes plus double dashes can randomly spawn ~8k damage on the urn.

Still way too good — the second-best tank — with huge early and whole-game value, the strongest hero at minutes 5/10/15. A DPS tank that dives backlines and wins duels; he isn't AoE but is the non-AoE hero you still want.
The ultimate potential man — great urn value and parry/bolt utility, but too inconsistent to be S without a draft (you can coin-flip into ~80% unfavorable matchups). Mid-A is a high placement.
Phenomenal — a huge fan of the grenade build. Ult max, grenades on mid boss, and grenades on a stacked urn give built-in anti-heal; one of the better M1 carries, ranked around/above Mirage.
Really good even after a nerf ('pretty LAR'). A gun hero with good early tempo; his death on the urn is a giga equalizer because he stuns for ages and amps allied AoE. Sleeper S-tier.
Garbage — a victim hero; playing her into Lash/Paradox every game is miserable. Slightly more urn utility than some but still junk.

Garbage and got worse. Mid-lane is the worst terrain for him, ball/splatter do nothing, and the punch buff is effectively a nerf because Rebuttal has the highest buy rate of any patch, making him damage himself.
Hella good — possibly S. Strong early and his ult is really valuable on the urn, held back only by the variance of being random-drafted into Lash/Billy.
The big loser — called F-tier / possibly the worst hero in the game. The gun-damage direction (Yoshi) is bad, no AoE nuking, was already bad last patch.
Chill and pretty good — the best carry at deleting AoE slop. Ricochet Wraith makes Graves unplayable and does giga late AoE damage. Probably high placement.

Good regardless of doubters. Her 2 gives 40 free spirit plus spirit-per-boon, letting her skip purple items, yet her one hits 700 (1,300 with Tankbuster+Reverb) while she's invulnerable for urn fights; scaling went from ~1.8-1.9 to 2.1-2.6.

Combined with Reverb pushes Yamato's one to ~1,300 damage.
With Tankbuster, boosts Yamato's one damage to ~1,300.
~5 per team per game in high ELO, cleansing Infernus burns/debuffs and gutting his value.
The new Arctic Blast changes let Shiv produce ~8k random urn damage with double dashes.
Part of the theoretical Dynamo survival kit that doesn't fix his urn-fight problems.
Doesn't save Dynamo from McGinnis ult one-framing him.
Victor's hybrid path: rush ~6.4k gun spike early, then pivot to Improved Reach and green items.
The Magic Carpet buff is why Holliday is actually good/rising.
Cited sarcastically — chat claims it fixes Infernus; the creator dismisses it as meaningless in practice.

reasoning_patterns: Frames a global/system change as the real hero buff: the global health reduction plus Billy's Spirit Snatch buff is what makes one slam worth ~900 HP and Billy the best frontliner.
Reads the comeback urn (50% armor, 60m radius) as inverting the value of early-game comps — winning lane hard is a losing position, so a strong pre-10 hero like Apollo lands in C despite his numbers.
Tracks an item's buy rate as a balance lever: Rebuttal's record pick rate turns Viscous's punch buff into a self-damage nerf, i.e. a buff that is really a nerf.
Names a bug as temporary: Kelvin's ability to dome the urn is called a hotfix-in-48-hours bug and his placement is conditional on it being fixed, same for Lady Geist snapping back up.
Distinguishes pilot/ELO from kit strength: Seven and Graves swing wildly between low ELO (S+/OP) and Eternus (unpicked), so the tier is a comp read, not a raw power read.
Inferns intent from an omission: the biggest surprise is that Mirage received no nerf despite being giga-broken, showing the patch targeted the urn meta rather than raw single-target power.

patch_calls.headline: The urn is king: a comeback-urn system plus a global health reduction make urn teamfights the whole game, decided by minute 15-20.
non_obvious_calls: Mirage escaped nerfs entirely despite being the most broken hero — the patch targeted the urn, not raw power, leaving him giga-broken but placement-suppressed.
McGinnis's ult, not her turrets, is what's actually broken — maxed ult one-frames a full-HP Dynamo through Unstoppable.
Kelvin doming the urn is likely an unintended bug that will be hotfixed, meaning his (and Lady Geist's) tier is unstable within days.
Winning lane hard is a losing position because of the comeback urn, so early-game comps that stomp are punished in competitive.
Warden is called the worst hero in the game, worse than last patch, because the gun-damage direction gives him no AoE nuking.
Dynamo is a competitive no-pick (zero selections across regions) despite looking like the ideal urn hero — a signal that a 'broken' ult can be fully countered by better CC.
